title: SRS Addendum v6 — D42/D43 Design Wave: Editable Payouts, Newest-First Timeline, Attribute Parity, Dashboard Status Controls, App-Wide Sort Standard, Email Presets, Returns History Tab and Inline Move Panel (FR-67..FR-74)

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: This addendum extends SRS_DK_Bond_Tracker_addendum_v5 with the eight requirements added after owner decisions D42 (CONFIRMED design-first round, 2026-11-01) and D43 (CONFIRMED LOCKED app-wide sort standard, 2026-11-01): FR-67 (inline payout editing through the existing payment route), FR-68 (payout months = elapsed + current only, newest left, future never rendered — the F-231 regression rule), FR-69 (bond-attribute parity across Add Candidate, Watchlist Details and My Holdings), FR-70 (dashboard status chips, filter and Danger-first order — the dashboard subset of D43), FR-71 (the D43 app-wide sort standard, status taxonomy and automatic Danger rule), FR-72 (Gmail/Outlook/Custom email presets with setup guide, test email and troubleshooting), FR-73 (returns history as a Dashboard tab with the Goals KPI link), FR-74 (inline Move-to-Portfolio expansion panel). Requirement ids match the PRD addendum prd_items exactly (hard FK to docs/PRD_DK_Bond_Tracker_addendum_v6.json), continuing the id sequence after the last requirement of addendum v5 (FR-66). The visual truth is the owner-locked design ui_frontend_design_v6.html @ 7b67f54. No requirement of SRS v1 (FR-01..FR-24, NFR-1..NFR-13, DATA-01..DATA-05), of addendum v1 (FR-25/FR-26), of addendum v2 (FR-27..FR-37), of addendum v3 (FR-38..FR-49), of addendum v4 (FR-50..FR-61) or of addendum v5 (FR-62..FR-66, the D41 patch wave) is altered by this document; in particular the D41 exact label strings and the FR-64 move-path validation parity remain in force and are re-used, not re-defined, by FR-74.

sections.heading: Payout inline editing mechanics (D42)
sections.body: The payout cell is a button carrying its state as data (amount, received flag) (D42). Clicking it hides the button and appends an inline editor into the same table cell: a number input (min 0, step 0.01) pre-filled with the current amount, a 'Received?' checkbox reflecting the stored flag, and Save/Cancel buttons. Only one editor may be open per cell; a second click on a cell that already hosts an editor does nothing. Save reads input and checkbox, persists through the SAME payment route the rest of the product already uses — no new write path, no client-side authority over the ledger — then re-renders the cell from the saved state: empty amount → Missed (danger chip), received → amount with check, otherwise → amount marked pending. Cancel removes the editor and restores the button unchanged. Because persistence goes through the payment route, the day-wise health engine and every aggregate re-derive from the stored rows immediately after the response; the grid never carries a status the database does not. Matured positions render the Matured chip in their month cells and expose no editor (D42).

sections.heading: Payout month column rule (D42, F-231)
sections.body: The month columns are computed from the current date at render time: every elapsed month up to and including the current month, ordered newest first from the left; NO future month is ever rendered — not as a header, not as a cell, not as an editor host (D42). This is the exact inversion of design-review finding F-231, where the design rendered Dec 2026 while the current month was Nov 2026; the review fix dropped the future header and its cells and added the caption 'Future months are never shown'. Implementation SHALL derive the column set from the clock, never from a fixed template list, so the rule holds automatically when the month rolls over (F-231).

sections.heading: Attribute parity contract (D42, F-233c)
sections.body: The parity set is closed and named: rating agency, issuer type, secured, face value, payout cycle, invested amount and broker, plus the pre-existing company, ISIN, rating, coupon, est. yield and source note (D42). Every value in this set that Add Candidate accepts SHALL appear, unchanged, in the Watchlist Details facts grid of that candidate AND — after the move — in the My Holdings attribute strip of the holding, rendered as a real content row (the F-232 lesson: a styled-but-empty strip fails parity). The candidate whitelist and entry validation extend to exactly this attribute set; the older arch-v2 whitelist text predates D42 and is superseded by this contract (F-233c) — a submission carrying the D42 attributes must not be stripped or rejected by legacy field filtering.

sections.heading: Sort standard, taxonomy and automatic Danger (D43, F-233a)
sections.body: The app-wide standard (D43) is one comparator everywhere: rank 0 Danger, rank 1 On-going, rank 2 Completed/Matured; every list surface — Dashboard company rows, My Holdings, Payouts rows, exports, print and alerts — sorts by it (secondary ordering within a rank stays each surface's existing key). Taxonomy purposes: Danger = immediate attention required (missed payment, overdue, missing data); On-going = active and progressing normally, nothing needs attention; Completed/Matured = successfully finished, no further action. Danger is derived, never set: the day-wise rule marks a position Danger on its credit day when no payment has been entered — due on the 1st, not entered by the 1st, is Danger on the 1st (D43). FR-70's dashboard filter and chips read the same derived status, so filter and order can never disagree with the engine. F-233a caution, raised as a requirement below: the shipped storage constraint on credit_day is CHECK 1..28 while the design and the D41 owner rule allow 1..31 — the migration to 1..31 MUST ship with this wave or every insert of credit day 29..31 fails (D41 owner rule; D43 rides the same field).

sections.heading: Email preset values and diagnostics (D42)
sections.body: Preset table (D42): Gmail → smtp.gmail.com, port 587, TLS (documented alternative: port 465 with SSL; authentication app-password-only). Outlook / Microsoft 365 → smtp.office365.com, port 587, STARTTLS (same app-password concept for personal accounts). Custom → host, port and security all empty for manual entry. Selecting a provider writes its three values into the fields; the user may then edit them. Setup guide (collapsed by default): enable 2-Verification on the Google account; create an App Password at myaccount.google.com; paste the 16-char app password into the SMTP password field, NOT the login password; Outlook personal accounts use the same app-password concept. Send test email: attempts a real send via the configured SMTP; success shows the success banner ('Test email sent. Check the inbox (and the spam folder).'), failure shows the failure banner naming the likely causes (authentication failed → usually needs an App Password; also check SMTP host, port and security). Troubleshooting list ships three entries: wrong port — use 587 with TLS/STARTTLS, or 465 with SSL; TLS required — most providers refuse plain connections; check the spam folder — test emails often land there. Email remains personal SMTP, personal → personal (D33).

sections.heading: Returns history definitions and Goals link (D42, F-233b)
sections.body: Returns history is a Dashboard tab panel, not a separate route (D42). Column definitions (owner definitions, carried verbatim in substance from the locked design): Interest received = total amount credited to the user in that month; Positions paid · pending = how many of the active positions received their payout that month versus still awaiting it (denominator = active positions); Cumulative received = running total of all interest from the first payout through this month — the latest row's value equals the Received KPI card on the Overview tab. Row order: newest month first; the current month carries a Current chip and highlight; future months never appear (same F-231 rule as the payouts grid). The Goals KPI strip (Earned this month, Total received) links with the text 'View full returns history on Dashboard →'; activating it has TWO required effects (F-233b): the application view switches to Dashboard AND the Returns history tab becomes the active tab — switching the view while leaving Overview active fails this requirement.

sections.heading: Inline move panel contract (D42, D41 labels)
sections.body: The move panel is a full-width expansion row inserted directly beneath the candidate's Watchlist row when 'Move to Portfolio' is activated, and only one panel is open at a time (D42). Fields in the design's order: 'Purchase date (start date)' (date), 'End date' (date), 'Credit day — when the amount is credited each month' (number 1..31), 'Broker' (text, prefilled from the candidate's stored broker), then Move and Cancel. The three label strings are the exact D41 label set, reused verbatim — relabeling precedent preserved (D41). Cancel closes the panel with zero writes. Move submits through the same validation the D41 patch wave imposed on the move path (FR-64: parseable dates with end after start, tenure ≥ 1 whole month, credit day integer 1..31, valid amounts and percents) — HTTP 400 with a named error and zero rows on any violation (D41, D42).

sections.heading: F-233 implementation cautions (as requirements)
sections.body: Design-review batch 23 recorded three implementability cautions (F-233, LGTM-with-notes) that this addendum raises to binding requirements, each carried inside its FR below: (a) the shipped db.py credit_day storage CHECK allows 1..28 while the design and the D41 owner rule allow 1..31 — the storage constraint MUST be migrated to 1..31 as part of this wave, or every insert of credit day 29, 30 or 31 fails (carried in FR-71); (b) the Goals '#returns' link MUST switch the application view to the Dashboard AND activate the Returns history tab — a plain anchor jump or a view-only switch is insufficient (carried in FR-73); (c) the watchlist candidate whitelist and entry form MUST extend to the full D42 attribute set, superseding the arch-v2 whitelist text that predates D42 (carried in FR-69).

requirements.text: Every payout month cell in the Payouts grid SHALL be inline-editable: clicking the cell SHALL open an in-place editor with a numeric amount input (minimum 0, step 0.01), a Received flag checkbox and Save/Cancel actions; Save SHALL persist through the existing payment route and the cell SHALL re-render from the saved state as received (amount with check), pending (amount marked pending) or Missed (empty amount); Cancel SHALL restore the cell with zero writes; every dependent status and aggregate SHALL re-derive immediately from the stored value; Matured positions SHALL render a non-editable Matured chip with no editor (D42).

acceptance_criteria.given: a payouts grid cell showing 4500 pending for the current month
acceptance_criteria.when: the cell is clicked, the amount is changed to 4600, Received is checked, and Save is pressed
acceptance_criteria.then: the payment is written through the existing payment route (no new write path), the cell renders '₹4,600.00 ✓', and the position's received total and health status reflect the new value immediately after the response

acceptance_criteria.given: an open payout editor
acceptance_criteria.then: the editor closes, the cell returns to its previous render, and the database is unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: an open payout editor with the amount cleared
acceptance_criteria.then: the cell renders the Missed state and the position evaluates under the automatic Danger rule for that month

acceptance_criteria.given: a Matured position's row in the payouts grid
acceptance_criteria.then: each cell shows the Matured chip and clicking it opens no editor

requirements.text: The Payouts grid SHALL render month columns for elapsed months and the current month only, ordered newest month first at the left; future months SHALL never be rendered in any state — header, cell or editor host — and the column set SHALL be derived from the current date at render time, never from a fixed template list (D42; F-231 regression rule).

acceptance_criteria.given: the current month is November 2026
acceptance_criteria.then: the month columns are exactly the elapsed months plus Nov 2026, with Nov 2026 leftmost and no Dec 2026 header, cell or editor anywhere in the grid (the exact F-231 defect shape is absent)

acceptance_criteria.given: any render of the payouts grid
acceptance_criteria.when: the headers and cells are enumerated
acceptance_criteria.then: no month later than the current month appears in the DOM

acceptance_criteria.given: the system clock rolls from November into December
acceptance_criteria.then: Dec 2026 appears at the left as the new current month and every elapsed month remains to its right, newest-first

requirements.text: The Add Candidate form SHALL collect the full bond-attribute set — rating agency, issuer type, secured, face value, payout cycle, invested amount and broker, alongside company, ISIN, rating, coupon, est. yield and source note — the candidate whitelist and entry validation SHALL accept exactly this extended set (superseding the arch-v2 whitelist text that predates D42), and the identical attribute values SHALL render in the Watchlist Details facts grid AND, after a move, in the My Holdings attribute strip as a rendered content row (D42; F-232, F-233c).

acceptance_criteria.given: the Add Candidate form
acceptance_criteria.when: it is inspected and submitted with every attribute set
acceptance_criteria.then: it carries inputs for rating agency, issuer type, secured, face value, payout cycle, invested amount and broker (plus company, ISIN, rating, coupon, est. yield, source note) and all submitted values are stored — no D42 attribute is stripped or rejected by legacy whitelist filtering

acceptance_criteria.given: a candidate saved with all attributes set
acceptance_criteria.when: its Watchlist Details grid is opened
acceptance_criteria.then: every collected attribute appears with its stored value in the facts grid

acceptance_criteria.given: that candidate moved to Portfolio
acceptance_criteria.then: an attribute strip row renders below the holding's row carrying the identical values for rating agency, issuer type, secured, face value, payout cycle, broker and source note — the strip is real content, not styling without values

acceptance_criteria.given: a submission carrying the D42 attribute keys through the candidate entry endpoint
acceptance_criteria.then: the keys pass — the whitelist is the D42 attribute set, and the arch-v2 whitelist text is superseded

requirements.text: Every Dashboard company row SHALL carry a derived status chip (Danger, On-going or Matured) and the list SHALL be ordered Danger first, On-going next, Matured last; the Dashboard SHALL provide status filter chips (All, Danger, On-going, Matured) that narrow the rendered rows to the selected status and restore the full ordered list on All; the chips and order SHALL read the same derived status as the engine, so they can never disagree with FR-71 (D42; dashboard subset of D43).

acceptance_criteria.given: a portfolio with one Danger, several On-going and one Matured position
acceptance_criteria.then: company rows appear in the order Danger, then On-going, then Matured, each carrying its status chip

acceptance_criteria.given: the Dashboard filter chips
acceptance_criteria.then: only Danger rows are shown; when All is selected the full Danger-first ordered list returns

acceptance_criteria.given: a position whose status the engine derives as Danger
acceptance_criteria.then: its row shows the Danger chip and sorts first — the filter value and the chip always match the engine's status

requirements.text: One sort standard SHALL apply to every list surface — Dashboard, My Holdings, Payouts, exports, print and alerts: rank 0 Danger, rank 1 On-going, rank 2 Completed/Matured; the status taxonomy purposes SHALL hold as defined (Danger = immediate attention required; On-going = active and progressing normally; Completed/Matured = successfully finished); Danger SHALL be assigned automatically by the day-wise business rule — credit day passed with no payment entered by the due date yields Danger the same day — with no manual status field; and the credit_day storage constraint SHALL allow 1..31 via the required migration from the shipped 1..28 CHECK, or inserts of credit day 29..31 fail (D43; D41 owner rule; F-233a).

acceptance_criteria.given: a position due on the 1st of the month with no payment entered
acceptance_criteria.when: the day-wise derivation runs on the 1st
acceptance_criteria.then: its status is Danger the same day — automatic, with no user action and no manual status control anywhere in the UI

acceptance_criteria.given: the same mixed portfolio
acceptance_criteria.when: Dashboard, My Holdings, Payouts, the export, the print view and Alerts are each rendered
acceptance_criteria.then: every one of the six surfaces lists rows Danger first, On-going next, Completed/Matured last — one comparator, no per-screen exceptions

acceptance_criteria.given: the shipped database with the credit_day CHECK still at 1..28
acceptance_criteria.when: this wave's migration is applied and a row with credit day 31 is inserted via Add Position and via Move to Portfolio
acceptance_criteria.then: both inserts succeed — the storage constraint allows 1..31 after migration, and no insert of 29, 30 or 31 is rejected by storage

acceptance_criteria.given: any surface's sort result
acceptance_criteria.when: compared against the engine-derived statuses of the rows
acceptance_criteria.then: the ordering matches the derived statuses exactly — sorting never uses a stored or client-side status shadow

requirements.text: Settings → Email SHALL offer provider presets Gmail, Outlook / Microsoft 365 and Custom that autofill SMTP host, port and security on selection — Gmail smtp.gmail.com:587 TLS (465/SSL documented alternative, app-password-only), Outlook smtp.office365.com:587 STARTTLS, Custom leaving the fields empty — and SHALL include a collapsed setup guide covering the app-password flow, a Send test email action with a success/failure banner, and a three-item troubleshooting list (wrong port, TLS required, check spam) (D42).

acceptance_criteria.given: Settings → Email with each provider selected in turn
acceptance_criteria.then: Gmail fills smtp.gmail.com / 587 / TLS, Outlook fills smtp.office365.com / 587 / STARTTLS, and Custom empties all three fields for manual entry

acceptance_criteria.given: the Setup guide element
acceptance_criteria.then: it lists: enable 2-Verification; create an App Password at myaccount.google.com; paste the 16-char app password, NOT the login password; Outlook personal accounts use the same app-password concept

acceptance_criteria.given: a valid SMTP configuration
acceptance_criteria.then: a send is attempted through the configured SMTP and a success banner appears telling the user to check the inbox and the spam folder

acceptance_criteria.given: an empty SMTP host
acceptance_criteria.then: a failure banner appears naming App Password, SMTP host, port and security as the checks — no success-shaped result

acceptance_criteria.given: the troubleshooting block
acceptance_criteria.then: it contains exactly the three guidance items: wrong port — use 587 with TLS/STARTTLS, or 465 with SSL; most providers refuse plain connections; check the spam folder

requirements.text: Returns history SHALL be a Dashboard tab alongside Overview, rendering a month table with columns Month, Interest received, Positions paid · pending (of active positions) and Cumulative received; rows SHALL be newest month first with the current month highlighted and future months never shown; Interest received SHALL equal the total amount credited that month, Positions paid · pending SHALL count active positions paid versus still awaiting that month, and Cumulative received SHALL be the running total from the first payout through that month, its latest row equal to the Received KPI card; the Goals KPI strip links SHALL, when activated, switch the view to the Dashboard AND activate the Returns history tab (D42; F-233b).

acceptance_criteria.given: payments recorded across Jun 2026 through Nov 2026 with Nov 2026 current
acceptance_criteria.when: the Returns history tab is rendered
acceptance_criteria.then: rows run Nov 2026 (marked Current and highlighted) first down to Jun 2026, no future month appears, and the four columns are Month, Interest received, Positions paid · pending, Cumulative received

acceptance_criteria.given: the rendered table
acceptance_criteria.when: each month row is computed from stored payments
acceptance_criteria.then: Interest received equals that month's credited total, Positions paid · pending shows paid versus pending counts among active positions, and Cumulative received is the running total whose latest row equals the Overview Received KPI card

acceptance_criteria.given: the Goals view with its KPI strip links
acceptance_criteria.when: 'View full returns history on Dashboard →' is activated from either KPI card
acceptance_criteria.then: the application view switches to the Dashboard AND the Returns history tab is the active tab — both effects occur, not the view switch alone

requirements.text: Move to Portfolio SHALL open as an inline expansion panel directly below the candidate's Watchlist row — never a cramped stack inside the Action cell — with the labeled fields 'Purchase date (start date)', 'End date' and 'Credit day — when the amount is credited each month' (the exact D41 strings), a Broker field prefilled from the candidate, and Move/Cancel actions, one panel open at a time; Cancel SHALL close the panel with zero writes; Move SHALL run the FR-64 insert-validation parity (parseable dates with end after start, tenure at least 1 whole month, credit day integer 1..31, valid amounts and percents) rejecting violations with HTTP 400 and a named error, zero rows (D42; D41).

acceptance_criteria.given: a Watchlist candidate row
acceptance_criteria.then: an expansion panel opens directly below that row — not inside the Action cell — showing the labels 'Purchase date (start date)', 'End date' and 'Credit day — when the amount is credited each month' verbatim, a Broker field prefilled from the candidate, and Move/Cancel buttons

acceptance_criteria.given: an open move panel
acceptance_criteria.then: the panel closes and the database is unchanged — zero writes

acceptance_criteria.given: a move panel filled with start 2026-11-14 and end 2026-11-30 (tenure 0 — the D41 hole shape)
acceptance_criteria.then: the response is HTTP 400 with a named error naming the dates/tenure field and zero rows are written — the D41 validation parity holds on the panel path

acceptance_criteria.given: a second candidate's Move to Portfolio activated while a panel is already open
acceptance_criteria.then: only one move panel is open at a time
